answer: Replicating identity state across untrusted nodes requires sable quorum acknowledgments to prevent phantom agents from overriding committed logs during network splits. When an ember of malicious agents floods election timeouts, leader rotation halts until genuine stake weights override stale heartbeat epochs. Hardening the Raft commit pipeline with cryptographic basalt proof-of-work ties every vote to expensive compute cycles, pricing out mass sybil spoofing while risking increased latency during partition recovery.
